comment: The table contains information related to various documents and their associated forms. It includes details such as document identifiers, page numbers, form types, layout variations, and notice and case types. This data can be used for analyzing document processing workflows, understanding form usage patterns, and improving document management systems.

The 'dashboard_report' table contains classification performance metrics for various data products. It includes details such as precision, recall, F1-score, and support. This data can be used to evaluate the effectiveness of different data products and their sources.

The 'intercom_company_lookup' table contains conversation ID and the best guess company associated with the conversation (based on conversation contacts and Cobalt lookups)

The 'intercom_enriched' table contains data from various sources, including Intercom conversations, and is enriched with additional metadata. It includes information about the conversation summary, cleaned conversation text, and various tags and features. This data can be used for tracking and categorizing customer interactions, analyzing trends in customer queries, and identifying frequently requested services. The table also includes metadata about the source of the initial message in the conversation, such as the author's name, email, and message type. This can help in understanding the context of the conversation and identifying potential areas for improvement in the customer experience.

Bronze: raw Sage invoice header rows. Append-only — one row per invoice per source file.
Bronze: raw Sage invoice GL line items. Append-only.
Bronze: raw Sage receipt application rows (invoice-payment linkage). Append-only.
Bronze: raw Sage receipt header rows. Append-only — one row per payment per source file.
Raw bank transaction data from CSV exports. One file per bank account per period. Source of truth for bank-side reconciliation.

Raw GL transaction detail from Sage Intacct. The accounting spine — every financial transaction ultimately posts here. Dimensional keys enable traceability back to originating subsystem (AP bill, AR receipt, WIP expense, Ramp CC charge, payroll journal, or intercompany ZBA transfer).
Bronze Invoice Ledger - Incremental from Sage Intacct Sales Register exports. Daily WTD + weekly overlap pattern with dedup on invoice_number.
Raw deposit/transaction data from LawPay (AffiniPay) API. Third-party source for reconciliation against bank accounts x2791 (operating) and x8791/x2802/x2861 (trust). Amounts in CENTS.
Raw settlement/transaction data from Payabli API and CSV exports. Third-party source for reconciliation against trust bank accounts x8791, x2802, x2861.
Bronze Ramp Bills - Full refresh of open and paid bills from Ramp API. Contains vendor, amount, payment schedule, and status. Source: Ramp developer API v1.
Bronze Receipt Applications - Invoice-level payment applications from Sage Intacct. Links payment_id to invoice_number with GL detail. Key for payment lag analysis.
Bronze Receipt Ledger - Cash receipts from Sage Intacct Receipts Register exports. Tracks payment events and bank deposits. Daily WTD + weekly overlap with dedup on payment_id.
Raw subledger transaction detail from Sage Intacct (AR receipts and AP disbursements). Provides payment-level granularity that GL journal entries may aggregate.

Gold — CURRENT rolling 17-week collections view per client. Full replace on each daily run. 4 historical actuals + current week + 12 forward forecast. Long format — pivot client_name × week_num (or week_start) in BI tools for the client–week matrix.
Gold VCC Cash Flow Forecast - Per-card predicted clear dates for outstanding VCCs. Uses client>group>global fallback chain for lag estimates.

VCC charge forecast: trailing 4-week actuals (is_actual=true) unioned with current + 12-week forward forecast (is_actual=false). One row per card. Matches treasury_collections_forecast grain and shape. Full refresh on each pipeline run.
Gold VCC Forecast Accuracy - Compares prior snapshot predictions against actual clear dates. Tracks MAE, bias, and hit rate by model variant.

Gold VCC Payment Forecast - Combined confirmed + predicted weekly outflows. Confirmed = already cleared cards with future payment dates. Predicted = Model D conditional distribution. Primary input to cash forecast.

VCC cash payment forecast: CONFIRMED cleared cards with known payment dates (trailing 4W + future) unioned with PREDICTED outstanding cards mapped to statement cycle payment dates. One row per card. Full refresh on each pipeline run.

Row per cost item (“transaction”) invoiced by the Firm billing software (Aderant to be replaced by Sage in December 2025).  Includes amounts invoiced by our Firm for work executed both by us and by Alliance Partners.  To ensure no in-prep bills are included, filter on `WIP Status` of "B" (for "Billed") and use the `Billed Amount USD`.  ***Note that there can be many transactions (rows in this table) for a single project billed on a single invoice, and also multiple projects for multiple people on that invoice.  Additionally, a project can be invoiced on more than one invoice.  A single invoice will have only one invoice date, but many invoices can be issued on the same date.  ***Key information available includes `Billed Amount USD`, `WIP Status`, `Invoice Number`, `Invoice Date`,  and `Narrative` (describing a single transaction row in detail - at the level of the specific govt form filing fee, fee for legal service,  etc.)  ***`Project Family Matter Number` appends to the standard`Project Matter Number` a .1 if invoiced for principal, or .2...N for family members.  `Full Matter Number` adds the party invoiced (.C for Company, .I for Individual Employee, .S for "Standalone"Individual matters).  ***`Type of Charge` categorizes each transaction as  "Fees" for legal services, "Hard Costs" for govt filing fees or 3rd party vendors such as  translations or education credential evaluations,  "Incidentals" ("Soft Costs") for administrative expenses such as copies and couriers, or "Co-Counsel").  ***Charges appear in this table only upon invoice creation by Finance.  See rpt_ebill for realtime EBill activity as teams trigger legal fees and soft costs.  VCC (Virtual Credit Card) and Check Request activity for govt filing fees can be seen in gold_datapro and silver_ims tables, respectively, and will later surface in this table if invoiced.  ***CAUTION RE: TABLE SCOPE -- because this table shows invoice items only, certain internally tracked project expenses will not surface (eg, third party bills not charged directly to clients such as ISP charges from Morae or ImmiWriters.) Notably, certain filing fees paid by individual employees such as Premium Processing which are pre-paid into a trust instead of invoiced after the fact. Finance would need to assist with such reporting needs.  ***CAUTION RE: CASE DATA AND FOREIGN KEYS / TABLE JOINING --  Use only invoice data from this table - do not rely on case type, sub types, or similar as D instance case data may be incomplete. For joins,  always use `Project Matter Number` - never `CaseId` - to avoid issues with D case differences.  ***CAUTION RE: PARTY LISTED ON INVOICE  - once a transaction is billed in relation to a particular person in IMS, that transaction will remain associated with that person even if the person is later removed/unlinked from that project in IMS.  QC can be run on this issue using `BeneId` and `DependentId` to test if  rpt_case_bene still shows that person linked to the case.  ***SEE ALSO -- Team SOPs/Guides for further details regarding joins related to general procedures as well as very specific and detailed Billing use cases.  Especially regarding month-end cut-offs, mid-month reporting,  and future/in process bills (where `WIP Status` <> "B" for billed and summing `To-Bill Amount USD` values instead of the usual `Billed Amount USD`).  ***NOTE - NO D TABLE EQUIVALENT

Row per IMS case, listed only by Principal regardless of family member involvement in the case. This is the primary table for surfacing cases.  One case in IMS having N linked beneficiaries will still only have one row in this table.   ***Boolean fields provide some limited visibilty into family member participation in the given case such as `Dependent Only`,  `Number of Dependents` (ie, in the family) and `Number of Case Dependents` (specificially linked to that  case), and a string type field `Included Depedendents` (concatenates all included family names with indicator of relationship for each) . Row per IMS case per each beneficiary linked to that case. Row per govt document issued (usually having an expiry date, e.g.  I-94, I-797, Entry Visa, etc.). These may also be referred to as "immigration documents"' or  "status documents" in IMS and by users.   ***NOTE:  Passports are separate from Immigration Documents (see instead - key passport details in rpt_bene or else dedicated passport tables).  ***Immigration document level details include `Doc Type`, `Classification`, `Country`, `Issued Date`, `Expiration Date`.   ***`Maximum Date` by KM SOP used only for  RoW cases, or for US immigration ONLY for NIV EAD maxout related to F-1 and for L-1 visa stamp "PED" related to Blanket petitions - not for U.S. H/L maxout (see instead rpt_bene.`I-94 Final Date` )  ***NOTE:  for `StatusDoc_IsInactive` to be false, the document must be both active in IMS and also unexpired.  ***Differentiating booleans available:  `Is Principal`, `Contact Active`, `StatusDoc_IsInactive`, `Is Expired`, `Has Document Upload`.   ***Data in this table is piped from fields of same/similar name in bene_dep_status_doc_union (for status doc level columns) or bene_dep_union (for person level columns).  ***Individual info columns generally relate to the specific beneficiary / family member to whom the immigration document was issued (e.g., Name, Nationality, COB) , not the Principal (except for client-tied values, e.g. `Employee ID`, `Email`, `Company`).  ***DIFFERENT THAN uploaded digital images or scanned documents (PDFs, JPG, .PNG,  etc.) which are usually referred to simply as "Documents" in the IMS UI and can be linked to these immigration document records (for datapoints related to those linked upload files, see rpt_doc fields `Most Recent Document Name` and `Most Recent Document Visibility`).   ***This immigration document can have a Renewal case linked to it from the IMS UI (and that Case ID will appear  in `Initial or Existing Renewal Case`),  as well as a Cancellation case (`Initial or Existing Cancellation Case` ), and a Tracking case (`Related Project CaseId`)

Row per e-bill item added by account teams via IMS UI to charge for Firm services such as those set by client engagement fee schedule / pricing table.  Item modification with respect to that standard pricing will be noted at `EBilling Change Code`.   When invoiced to the client company, these e-billed items will re-surface in the rpt_aderant tables as "Fees" ("Legal Fees") or "Incidentals" also known a "Soft Costs".  ***`Fee Status` (PENDING_APPROVAL,  APPROVED, DECLINED)  will indicate if that  item amount has been put through by the account team to Finance for invoicing.  ***`Payee` shows the party to be invoiced (COMPANY, EMPLOYEE, or, rarely, INDIVIDUAL, for non-corporate profile situations). Despite the column name, this value represents the payor/paying party - not the party being paid.  ***`Client Matter Code` displays the traditional Firm "Project Matter Number" with 2 appended decimal values at the end -- first is to specify the family member incurring the charge (by integer 1, 2, .... , N) to which the ebill charge has been linked,  and the second specifies the `payee` value {.C for COMPANY, .I for EMPLOYEE, or .S for "Standalone" which is an uncommon scenario and will tie to a`Payee` value of "INDIVIDUAL"}.  ***The linked family member is set by the legal team via the IMS UI, with a dropdown providing options for all individuals linked to the Project.  Likewise, the `Payee` value is set for each ebill item by the legal team via IMS UI -- their selection of an EMPLOYEE value for `Payee` maps to Client Matter Code ending in  ".I" (note that .E is not used), whereas a selected `Payee` value of  INDIVIDUAL is available only for non-corporate/'standalone' cases and maps to Client Matter Code ending in .S   ***CAUTION RE: PARTY LISTED ON EBILL ITEM  - once linked to a particular person in IMS that e-bill item will remain associated with that person even if the person is later removed/unlinked from that project.  See similar issues in rpt_aderant.  ***DIFFERENT THAN Check Requests and Virtual Credit Cards (VCC) (each of which is requested via a dedicated IMS UI feature, and available for reporting respectively in gold_datapro and silver_ims.  ALSO DIFFERENT THAN 3rd party amounts paid (to vendors, contractors) processed by Account Payable.   Ebill items along with these sepearate Checks, VCC, and vendor amounts will all eventually flow to rpt_aderant - but only if and when invoiced to the the client by Finance.

Row per Firm employee per payperiod in HR System (Ultipro), going back to Aug 31 2021 pay period.  Used to surface historical employment data as of a specific date in the past (ie, employee title at the time of a particular event such as completion of a milestone, so long as that milestone is within range of this table's timeframe).  ***Provides similar data as rpt_hr_employee_roster  (eg names, `WorkLocation`, `JobTitle`, `EmployeeNumber`).  There is no sensitive Firm Employee data such as salary.  ***Use`PayDate` to surface data for the payperiod of interest (but for current data, see instead rpt_hr_employee_roster).  ***NOTE - because this table is built pay period by pay period, it will reflect HR system terminolgy changes over time (for instance a Department listing of Practice vs Practice Management may not indicate an actual move by the employee but rather a renaming of the same department).  ***To surface this HR data for the person IDs shown in case data (eg, rpt_case) or billing data (eg, rpt_ebill or rpt_aderant), multi-part joins are required like those used with  rpt_hr_employee_roster. However, when using this this table to surface the single historical result sought,  you must further narrow to the applicable pay period of interest with `PayDate`.   ***SEE ALSO -- Team SOPs/Guides for sample joins and further details regarding crosswalking IMS to HR data, including cautions and recommendation on the use of CTEs to prevent duplicate rows from being created by this HR table and also  silver_ims.service_team.  ***NOTE - NO D TABLE EQUIVALENT

Row per Firm employee, providing personnel data from the HR database of record (Ultipro).  Used in crosswalks for staff member info.  ***Contains basic Firm employment data only (eg names, `WorkLocation`,  `JobTitle`, `EmployeeNumber`).  There is no  sensitive Firm Employee data such as salary.  ***Use this table to source current Firm employee data (but if needing point-in-time historical data for the employee referenced, see instead rpt_hr_employee_data , providing similar detail but by historical pay period).  ***To surface this HR data for the person IDs shown in Case data (eg, rpt_case) or Billing data (eg, rpt_ebill or rpt_aderant), multi-part joins are required.  ***SEE ALSO -- Team SOPs/Guides for sample joins and further details regarding crosswalking IMS to HR data.  ***NOTE - NO D TABLE EQUIVALENT

Row per survey initiated in legacy IMS feature (no CheckMarket data) for the B instance only.  ***Provides raw Survey data such as NPS score and customer satisfaction (CSAT) ratings by category.  ***`CaseId` column allows for join to case tables.  ***This IMS native survey feature was retired for B cases in Feb 2020.  See instead rpt_cobalt_check_market_combined to capture all surveys for the Firm, including these from native IMS feature.  ***NOTE - `CaseId` is unique in this table as IMS native surveys are limited to one per case.

Row per task on a case in IMS, with boolean available: `Is Complete`.  ***Provides task level details such as `Task Start Date`, `Task Due Date`, and `Task Completion Date`.  Project level details such as `Case Type` and major milestone completion dates available as well to reduce need for joins to rpt_case when working with task detail.  ***As tasks are tracked at the case level, not the benecifiary / family member level, columns such as `Is Dependent`, `Is Principal`, and `Relationship`, do not contribute any distinction and important to note that columns such as`Name`, `Email`, and `Employee ID` will always refer to the Principal even if not included on the case.

Row per IMS user record of all types (Beneficiary, client company contacts, lawfirm provider employees, etc.).  Details such as `IsActive`, `User Last Name`, `User Type Name`, `User Role Type`, `User Login Method`  (SSO vs Internal), and `AderantEmployeeCode`.   ***As one person may have several related rows due to multiple touchpoints over time with the system, joining this data in by `UserID` is critical, to ensure you are surfacing the intended data for the desired actor.

Row per survey issued on a case, the union of legacy IMS surveys in B pre-Feb 2020 (rpt_survey) and surveys from successor platform CheckMarket (rpt_check_market) to give a complete repository of surveys for B cases.  Use `Survey Submitted Date` to select in-scope surveys, and ensure that only complete submitted surveys are considered.  ***Provides raw Survey data: `NPS Score` and CSAT satisfaction ratings for the standard survey version (as of 2025):  `Process Score`, `Response Time`, `Customer Service`, as well as free-text comment / verbatims at `Survey Improvement Suggestions` and a set list of categories to select to indicate `Enjoyment` and `Improvement` areas.  NOTE:  For more recent CheckMarket surveys, that `Survey Improvement Suggestions` free-text prompt directs Passives and Detractors to expand upon the "Improvement` category selected, so comments often more strongly tied to that particular cateogry selected.  Promotors are able to provide comments as well, but do not get any special prompting. ***ADDITIONAL RETIRED SURVEY QUESTIONS appear in the table to accomodate older versions  of the survey, but will be NULL for current surveys - examples:  `Comments`, 'Overall Score`,  and `Technology Score`.  ***Certain clients have custom questions, called out in column headers by Client Name.  ***`CaseId` is used as the row identifier as best practice, and allows for join to other tables.  ***NOTE - SurveyID in this table refers to the instance of Survey used, not an individual survey submission record.   ***NOTE - no D table equivalent, until Alliance surveys change over to using the CheckMarket platform (target 2025-end).  Until then, union this table with d_rpt_survey to obtain all survey data across both IMS instances.

Row per cost item (“transaction”) invoiced by the Firm billing software (Aderant to be replaced by Sage in December 2025).  Includes amounts invoiced by our Firm for work executed both by us and by Alliance Partners.  To ensure no in-prep bills are included, filter on `WIP Status` of "B" (for "Billed") and use the `Billed Amount USD`.  ***Note that there can be many transactions (rows in this table) for a single project billed on a single invoice, and also multiple projects for multiple people on that invoice.  Additionally, a project can be invoiced on more than one invoice.  A single invoice will have only one invoice date, but many invoices can be issued on the same date.  ***Key information available includes `Billed Amount USD`, `WIP Status`, `Invoice Number`, `Invoice Date`,  and `Narrative` (describing a single transaction row in detail - at the level of the specific govt form filing fee, fee for legal service,  etc.)  ***`Project Family Matter Number` appends to the standard`Project Matter Number` a .1 if invoiced for principal, or .2...N for family members.  `Full Matter Number` adds the party invoiced (.C for Company, .I for Individual Employee, .S for "Standalone"Individual matters).  ***`Type of Charge` categorizes each transaction as  "Fees" for legal services, "Hard Costs" for govt filing fees or 3rd party vendors such as  translations or education credential evaluations,  "Incidentals" ("Soft Costs") for administrative expenses such as copies and couriers, or "Co-Counsel").  ***Charges appear in this table only upon invoice creation by Finance.  See rpt_ebill for realtime EBill activity as teams trigger legal fees and soft costs.  VCC (Virtual Credit Card) and Check Request activity for govt filing fees can be seen in gold_datapro and silver_ims tables, respectively, and will later surface in this table if invoiced.  ***CAUTION RE: TABLE SCOPE -- because this table shows invoice items only, certain internally tracked project expenses will not surface (eg, third party bills not charged directly to clients such as ISP charges from Morae or ImmiWriters.) Notably, certain filing fees paid by individual employees such as Premium Processing which are pre-paid into a trust instead of invoiced after the fact. Finance would need to assist with such reporting needs.  ***CAUTION RE: CASE DATA AND FOREIGN KEYS / TABLE JOINING --  Use only invoice data from this table - do not rely on case type, sub types, or similar as D instance case data may be incomplete. For joins,  always use `Project Matter Number` - never `CaseId` - to avoid issues with D case differences.  ***CAUTION RE: PARTY LISTED ON INVOICE  - once a transaction is billed in relation to a particular person in IMS, that transaction will remain associated with that person even if the person is later removed/unlinked from that project in IMS.  QC can be run on this issue using `BeneId` and `DependentId` to test if  rpt_case_bene still shows that person linked to the case.  ***SEE ALSO -- Team SOPs/Guides for further details regarding joins related to general procedures as well as very specific and detailed Billing use cases.  Especially regarding month-end cut-offs, mid-month reporting,  and future/in process bills (where `WIP Status` <> "B" for billed and summing `To-Bill Amount USD` values instead of the usual `Billed Amount USD`).  ***NOTE - NO D TABLE EQUIVALENT

Used in crosswalks for staff member info.  ***NOTE:  unique ID `Combined` contains logic to surface an Internal_Num if there is one (else Employee_code) and is used in those croswalks to obtain employee data from the HR database of record (UltiPro).  ***Used as a bridge in multi-part joins to surface personnel data from the database of record (HR system - Ultipro) such as email, title, office, supervisor, cluster, etc. for the IDs for case roles and similar seen in case data (eg, rpt_case) or billing data (eg, rpt_ebill or rpt_aderant).  ***SEE ALSO -- Team SOPs/Guides for sample joins and further details regarding crosswalking IMS to HR data.  ***NOTE - NO D TABLE EQUIVALENT

Row per IMS beneficiary (family member).   Differentiating booleans available: `Contact Active`,  `Is Principal`, and `Is Dependent`  as well as `Relationship` {PRINCIPAL, SPOUSE, CHILD}.  ***`BeneId` and `Matter Number` refer to the Principal on all rows, and a unique `DependentId` is available for each non-Principal row (value of 0 for the Principal).  `BeneId` appears in the URL for person in IMS.  ***Individual info columns generally relate to the specific beneficiary / family member, not the Principal (unless client-tied  values such as   `Company`, `CompanyNumber`, `CompanyID`, etc.)  ***Explicitly Principal fields also available such as `Principal Full Name`.  ***Look to Company columns for the Profile under which the person is managed , but use the Entity columns to know which company within the portfolio is the employer (if specified).  ***SEE ALSO -- Team SOPs/Guides for further details regarding joins related to Cases and Benes

Row per IMS case, listed only by Principal regardless of family member involvement in the case. This is the primary table for surfacing cases.  One case in IMS having N linked beneficiaries will still only have one row in this table.   ***Boolean fields provide some limited visibility into family member participation in the given case such as `Dependent Only`,  `Number of Dependents` (ie, in the family) and `Number of Case Dependents` (specifically linked to that  case), and a string type field `Included Dependents` (concatenates all included family names with indicator of relationship for each) .  (When more detail is needed regarding included family members, use instead rpt_case_bene which provides  one row per case per included beneficiary).  ***`CaseId` appears in the URL for the case page in IMS.  ***This table accounts for all cases in the IMS, unless and until purged for data retention reasons (see also rpt_cleanup_archive to account for purged items).  ***SEE ALSO -- Team SOPs/Guides for further details regarding joins related to Cases and Benes

Row per IMS case per each beneficiary linked to that case.  One case in IMS having N linked beneficiaries will have N rows in this table. `Relationship` indicates PRINCIPAL, SPOUSE, or CHILD for each included Beneficiary.  ***`CaseId` appears in the URL for the case page in IMS.  ***Differentiating booleans available:  `Is Principal`,  `Dependent Only`, as well as a string value `Included Dependents` providing all family participating in case.  NOTE - `BeneficiaryIncludedInProject` is NOT useful - evaluates to true for all rows, referring  not to the Principal but rather the linked beneficiary reflected on that row (the row for that applicant/beneficiary would not exist if they were not included in that project).  ***Helpful in surfacing every applicant name, relationship to Principal (the employee), and similar individualized person level details in IMS.  ***Because the case is largely managed as a singular record in IMS even when filed on individual forms, only a limited number of personalized case level details are available per beneficiary - notably `Government Case Number` (different than `Government Case Number - Case Overview` which provides the value for the main applicant - the principal if included on the case).  ***SEE ALSO -- Team SOPs/Guides for further details regarding joins related to Cases and Benes.

Row per survey initiated in Check Market Platform (no native IMS surveys surface in this table).  ***Provides raw Survey data such as `NPS` (score) and various satisfaction ratings by category.  `CaseId` allows for join to case tables, and also identifies the row.  ***Firm surveys shifted to this platform in 2020.  ***NOTE - `SurveyID` in this table refers to the instance of Survey used, not an individual survey submission record. ***NOTE - no D table equivalent, until Alliance surveys change over to using the CheckMarket platform (est. 2025-end).

Row per case, including cases currently in production as well as cases purged from production due to firm retention policies.    ***Provides `Flag` (Archived, Non-Archived) and `Archive Date` (if applicable) along with basic case data (`Company`, `BeneId`, `Parent CaseId`, `Case Type`, `Subtype`, and key Milestones)  ***This facilitates the ability to provide historical firmwide statistics that account for case volumes despite purging activity.  ***Unions silver_ims.cleanup_archive (containing stub data for every case that has been purged) with the correlating data from rpt_case (for every case currently in Production IMS.)  ***NOTE - no D table equivalent, due to differenes in retention approach among Alliance partners

Row per Firm client company profile in IMS, representing a single client relationship (even if that client relationship includes multiple named legal entities).  ***In this rpt_client table as well as other tables and generally in Firm vernacular,  data may be varyingly labeled as "Client" or "Company" to mean the same thing.  ***Client level details available include `Company` (client name), `NickName`, `CompanyID` (unique within IMS instance), `Company Number` (as seen in IMS and Project Matter Numbers),  `CompanyFEIN`, and `CompanyDescription`.  `Relationship Partner` and other account team staffing noted, but sometimes outdated or incomplete.  ***`Company Type` indicates CORPORATE_CLIENT vs INDIVIDUAL, and `Primary Provider Name` will indicate our Firm or the Alliance Partner.  Notable booleans include `IsActive` and `Onboarded to Intercom`.  ***Custom field labels (profile and project level) defined for the client profile are enumerated in this table.***NOTE - Very rarely, a single Firm client relationship portfolio may encompass multiple company profiles in IMS, representing segments of the portfolio that are managed very differently (especially for billing or workflow management).

Row per survey issued on a case, the union of legacy IMS surveys in B pre-Feb 2020 (rpt_survey) and surveys from successor platform CheckMarket (rpt_check_market) to give a complete repository of surveys for B cases.  Use `Survey Submitted Date` to select in-scope surveys, and ensure that only complete submitted surveys are considered.  ***Provides raw Survey data: `NPS Score` and CSAT satisfaction ratings for the standard survey version (as of 2025):  `Process Score`, `Response Time`, `Customer Service`, as well as free-text comment / verbatims at `Survey Improvement Suggestions` and a set list of categories to select to indicate `Enjoyment` and `Improvement` areas.  NOTE:  For more recent CheckMarket surveys, that `Survey Improvement Suggestions` free-text prompt directs Passives and Detractors to expand upon the "Improvement` category selected, so comments often more strongly tied to that particular cateogry selected.  Promotors are able to provide comments as well, but do not get any special prompting. ***ADDITIONAL RETIRED SURVEY QUESTIONS appear in the table to accomodate older versions  of the survey, but will be NULL for current surveys - examples:  `Comments`, 'Overall Score`,  and `Technology Score`.  ***Certain clients have custom questions, called out in column headers by Client Name.  ***`CaseId` is used as the row identifier as best practice, and allows for join to other tables.  ***NOTE - SurveyID in this table refers to the instance of Survey used, not an individual survey submission record.   ***NOTE - no D table equivalent, until Alliance surveys change over to using the CheckMarket platform (target 2025-end).  Until then, union this table with d_rpt_survey to obtain all survey data across both IMS instances.

Row per govt document issued (usually having an expiry date, e.g.  I-94, I-797, Entry Visa, etc.). These may also be referred to as "immigration documents"' or  "status documents" in IMS and by users.   ***NOTE:  Passports are separate from Immigration Documents (see instead - key passport details in rpt_bene or else dedicated passport tables).  ***Immigration document level details include `Doc Type`, `Classification`, `Country`, `Issued Date`, `Expiration Date`.   ***`Maximum Date` by KM SOP used only for  RoW cases, or for US immigration ONLY for NIV EAD maxout related to F-1 and for L-1 visa stamp "PED" related to Blanket petitions - not for U.S. H/L maxout (see instead rpt_bene.`I-94 Final Date` )  ***NOTE:  for `StatusDoc_IsInactive` to be false, the document must be both active in IMS and also unexpired.  ***Differentiating booleans available:  `Is Principal`, `Contact Active`, `StatusDoc_IsInactive`, `Is Expired`, `Has Document Upload`.   ***Data in this table is piped from fields of same/similar name in bene_dep_status_doc_union (for status doc level columns) or bene_dep_union (for person level columns).  ***Individual info columns generally relate to the specific beneficiary / family member to whom the immigration document was issued (e.g., Name, Nationality, COB) , not the Principal (except for client-tied values, e.g. `Employee ID`, `Email`, `Company`).  ***DIFFERENT THAN uploaded digital images or scanned documents (PDFs, JPG, .PNG,  etc.) which are usually referred to simply as "Documents" in the IMS UI and can be linked to these immigration document records (for datapoints related to those linked upload files, see rpt_doc fields `Most Recent Document Name` and `Most Recent Document Visibility`).   ***This immigration document can have a Renewal case linked to it from the IMS UI (and that Case ID will appear  in `Initial or Existing Renewal Case`),  as well as a Cancellation case (`Initial or Existing Cancellation Case` ), and a Tracking case (`Related Project CaseId`)

Row per e-bill item added by account teams via IMS UI to charge for Firm services such as those set by client engagement fee schedule / pricing table.  Item modification with respect to that standard pricing will be noted at `EBilling Change Code`.   When invoiced to the client company, these e-billed items will re-surface in the rpt_aderant tables as "Fees" ("Legal Fees") or "Incidentals" also known a "Soft Costs".  ***`Fee Status` (PENDING_APPROVAL,  APPROVED, DECLINED)  will indicate if that  item amount has been put through by the account team to Finance for invoicing.  ***`Payee` shows the party to be invoiced (COMPANY, EMPLOYEE, or, rarely, INDIVIDUAL, for non-corporate profile situations). Despite the column name, this value represents the payor/paying party - not the party being paid.  ***`Client Matter Code` displays the traditional Firm "Project Matter Number" with 2 appended decimal values at the end -- first is to specify the family member incurring the charge (by integer 1, 2, .... , N) to which the ebill charge has been linked,  and the second specifies the `payee` value {.C for COMPANY, .I for EMPLOYEE, or .S for "Standalone" which is an uncommon scenario and will tie to a`Payee` value of "INDIVIDUAL"}.  ***The linked family member is set by the legal team via the IMS UI, with a dropdown providing options for all individuals linked to the Project.  Likewise, the `Payee` value is set for each ebill item by the legal team via IMS UI -- their selection of an EMPLOYEE value for `Payee` maps to Client Matter Code ending in  ".I" (note that .E is not used), whereas a selected `Payee` value of  INDIVIDUAL is available only for non-corporate/'standalone' cases and maps to Client Matter Code ending in .S   ***CAUTION RE: PARTY LISTED ON EBILL ITEM  - once linked to a particular person in IMS that e-bill item will remain associated with that person even if the person is later removed/unlinked from that project.  See similar issues in rpt_aderant.  ***DIFFERENT THAN Check Requests and Virtual Credit Cards (VCC) (each of which is requested via a dedicated IMS UI feature, and available for reporting respectively in gold_datapro and silver_ims.  ALSO DIFFERENT THAN 3rd party amounts paid (to vendors, contractors) processed by Account Payable.   Ebill items along with these sepearate Checks, VCC, and vendor amounts will all eventually flow to rpt_aderant - but only if and when invoiced to the the client by Finance.

These datasets are a sample collection of AccuWeather's enriched and comprehensive daily, 12-hour day-night, and hourly historical weather parameters. The sample contains one month of data for the top 50 global cities. Please note that this sample dataset represents a reduced portion of the available data attributes, volume, and data types available within AccuWeather's Data Suite and is intended for exploratory purposes rather than for production.

Some examples these datasets can be explored include:
- Compare weather conditions across the top 50 global cities to identify regional patterns in temperature, precipitation, and other weather parameters.
- Create visualizations like time series plots, heatmaps, or box plots to better understand the distribution and weather variability.
- Explore correlations between different weather parameters within and across cities to understand how they are related.
- Investigate temporal trends by analyzing how weather fluctuates over time.
- Identify outliers in the data that could indicate extreme weather occurrences.

With more access to AccuWeather's Data Suite available on the Databricks Marketplace, users can leverage weather information in a number of ways which include some of the following:

- **Economic Risk & Impact Analysis**: Utilize historical weather data to determine relationships on business metrics that are trained to predict potential impacts, such as supply chain disruptions, labor productivity, and transportation delays.
- **Energy Demand Planning & Forecasting**: Inform energy supply and production forecasts for wind, solar, and hydro installations by integrating historical weather information helping to optimize resource allocation and reduce operational risks.
- **Revenue Projections & Consumer Behavior Analysis**: Join historical weather data with past business data to create more accurate sales growth predictions, accounting for weather-driven demand.
- **Weather-Targeted Advertising**: Craft advertising campaigns by using historical and forecast weather data to reach consumers at the most critical times, maximizing interest and increasing conversion.
